full_text_en:
Guangdong Dabao Property Management Co., Ltd. v.

Guangdong Zhongdai Enterprise Group Co., Ltd., Guangdong Zhongdai Telecommunications

Industry Co., Ltd., and Guangzhou Zhongshan Industrial Co., Ltd.

— Dispute over Equity Transfer Cooperation

【Ruling Gist】

1. In an equity transfer contract, even if both parties agree that the equity to be transferred is owned by a third party outside the contract, as long as the agreement only obligates one party to transfer the equity to the other party without actually causing a change in the rights of the equity owner, the equity transfer contract cannot be determined as a contract of unauthorized disposition and thus invalid on the ground that the transferor lacks the right to dispose of the equity.

2. After entering into a contract, a party wishing to rescind the contract must raise the matter with the other party. If the rescinding party does not raise the matter with the other party but instead agrees with a third party in another contract to rescind the former contract, the effect of rescission does not occur.

3. Liquidated damages are an agreement between the parties to a contract on the amount of damages payable by the defaulting party when contractual obligations are not performed. Therefore, liquidated damages exist for a specific obligation. This specific obligation may be a particular obligation in the contract, or it may be any obligation of either party under the contract. The court must first accurately determine the content of the obligation to which the liquidated damages pertain. After such determination, it must also examine whether that obligation has actually arisen. In commercial contracts, parties often attach preconditions to contractual obligations. When the conditions are not fulfilled, the contractual obligation does not actually exist, and there is no issue of performance. In such cases, the liquidated damages clause agreed upon for that obligation cannot be applied.

4. If a third party outside the contract promises the creditor in the contract to assume the debtor's obligations, in the absence of sufficient evidence that the creditor consented to the transfer of the debt to the third party or that the debtor withdrew from the contractual relationship, it should not be readily concluded that a debt transfer has occurred; generally, it should be considered a joinder of debt. After a third party indicates to the creditor its intention to join the debt, even if the creditor does not explicitly express consent, as long as the creditor has not explicitly objected or expressed objection through conduct, it should still be determined that a joinder of debt has been established, and the creditor may assert its rights against the third party in accordance with the relationship of joinder of debt.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2010) Min Ti Zi No. 153

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Guangdong Zhongdai Enterprise Group Co., Ltd. Address: No. 698, Renmin Bei Road, Yuexiu District, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Chang Jianguo, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Li Xiaozhong, lawyer of Beijing Shanggong Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Guangdong Zhongdai Telecommunications Industry Co., Ltd. Address: Unit 3, First Floor, South Side of Friendship Theatre, No. 696 Renmin Bei Road, Yuexiu District, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Chang Jianguo, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Liu Jianhai, lawyer of Beijing Shanggong Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Guangzhou Zhongshan Industrial Co., Ltd. Address: Second Floor, No. 36-38, Binjiang Xi Road, Haizhu District, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Weishan, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Li Jingwei, employee of the company.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Guangdong Dabao Property Management Co., Ltd. Address: No. 9, Liuhua Road, Yuexiu District, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Shaohuan, Executive Director.

Agent ad litem: Guan Wei, lawyer of Guangdong Zhongtian Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Tao, lawyer of Guangzhou Jinpeng Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over equity transfer cooperation between the Appellants, Guangdong Zhongdai Enterprise Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongdai Group Company), Guangdong Zhongdai Telecommunications Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongdai Telecom Company), and Guangzhou Zhongshan Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongshan Company), and the Respondent, Guangdong Dabao Property Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dabao Company), the Appellants, dissatisfied with the judgment of the Guangdong High People's Court (2007) Yue Gao Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 165, petitioned this Court for a retrial. This Court rendered a civil ruling on December 16, 2009, (2008) Min Er Jian Zi No. 21-1, granting a retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Wang Dongmin serving as the presiding judge, and acting judges Wang Fubo and Du Jun participating in the trial. Court Clerk Shang Min served as the recorder. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

On September 8, 2006, Dabao Company filed a lawsuit with the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court, requesting: 1. Rescission of the "Equity Transfer Cooperation Agreement of Guangzhou Zhongshan Industrial Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Cooperation Agreement") entered into by Dabao Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company; 2. An order that Zhongdai Telecom Company, Zhongshan Company, and Zhongdai Group Company return RMB 30 million to Dabao Company, pay capital costs (compensation for losses) of RMB 22.85 million, and pay overdue payment interest (calculated on a principal of RMB 52.85 million at the overdue loan interest rate of the bank, from February 23, 2006, to the actual date of repayment, provisionally calculated until the date of filing as RMB 2,158,000), totaling RMB 55,008,000.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court found in the first instance: On December 12, 2005, Dabao Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company entered into the Cooperation Agreement, stipulating: The three parties would use the restructured Zhongshan Company as a business platform to jointly carry out real estate development on the target land parcel; the premise and basis for cooperation was that Zhongdai Telecom Company promised that it had the right to dispose of 100% of the equity of Zhongshan Company, and Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company promised that Zhongshan Company had no external creditor's rights or debts. Shareholders Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong unconditionally transferred the use rights of the Pazhou PZB1301 land parcel (i.e., the target land parcel) under the "Guangzhou State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract" [Sui Guo Di Chu He (2005) No. 133] to Zhongshan Company. The equity value of Zhongshan Company was RMB 493.8 million (including land transfer fee of RMB 460 million, registered capital of RMB 20 million, and deed tax of RMB 13.8 million). Zhongdai Telecom Company transferred 10% of its 100% equity interest in Zhongshan Company to Dabao Company. The payment method for the equity transfer price was: Before December 13, 2005, Dabao Company paid the first installment of RMB 30 million, which was used to pay the land transfer fee for the target land parcel, with the balance to be paid in full by December 30, 2005. The agreement also stipulated that due to the need to pay the land transfer fee for the land parcel, Zhongdai Telecom Company hoped that Dabao Company could inject funds as soon as possible. Although the registration procedures for Dabao Company's 10% equity had been completed, this did not mean that the parties had reached agreement on the cooperation matters and the company's articles of association. Therefore, if the parties failed to reach an agreement on the cooperation matters within three months after the signing of this agreement (the cooperation parties formally signing an agreement on the cooperation matters concerning the target land parcel), Dabao Company had the right to withdraw from the cooperation. Zhongdai Telecom Company agreed to acquire Dabao Company's 10% shares in Zhongshan Company for RMB 52.85 million, and pay the full amount to Dabao Company immediately. If Zhongdai Telecom Company failed to perform as scheduled, Zhongdai Telecom Company agreed to pay liquidated damages to Dabao Company at a rate of 0.2% per day on the unfulfilled amount. Any party failing to fully perform this agreement shall bear liability for breach. The breaching party shall, in addition to compensating Zhongshan Company for losses, pay liquidated damages to the other shareholders at a rate of 0.2% per day on the amount in breach. Zhongshan Company provided comprehensive guarantees for Zhongdai Telecom Company's responsibilities and obligations under this agreement; if Zhongdai Telecom Company failed to fully perform this agreement, Zhongshan Company agreed to assume joint and several liability for all of Zhongdai Telecom Company's responsibilities and obligations under this agreement. On the same day, Zhongdai Group Company issued a "Letter of Commitment" to Dabao Company, stating: Due to the urgent need to pay the land transfer fee for the land parcel on December 13, 2005, Zhongdai Group Company hoped that Dabao Company would prepare RMB 30 million in advance before the cooperation matters between Zhongdai Group Company and Dabao Company were finalized, to ensure timely payment to the government for the land transfer fee. If the parties failed to reach an agreement on the cooperation matters, Dabao Company's losses in preparing the funds would be borne by Zhongdai Group Company. On December 13, 2005, Dabao Company paid RMB 30 million to Zhongshan Company, and Zhongshan Company immediately used the funds to pay the land transfer fee that Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong paid to the government.

Subsequently, because Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong violated the contract with the Guangzhou Bureau of Land Resources and Housing Administration (hereinafter referred to as Guangzhou Land Bureau) by failing to pay the land transfer fee on time, the Guangzhou Land Bureau rescinded the "Guangzhou State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract" entered into with Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, withdrew the Pazhou PZB1301 land parcel granted to Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, and re-listed it for public transfer at the Guangzhou Real Estate Transaction Registration Center on January 14, 2006.

On February 23, 2006, Dabao Company sent a letter to Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company, stating that because the target land parcel had been taken back by the government due to failure to pay the land transfer fee on time, it was impossible for the cooperation parties to reach an agreement on the cooperation matters. Therefore, Dabao Company requested to terminate the cooperation, and requested Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company to refund the funds to Dabao Company as soon as possible.

On June 9, 2006, Zhongdai Group Company issued a "Letter of Commitment" to Dabao Company, stating: The RMB 30 million that Dabao Company had previously paid for the state-owned land transfer fee would be repaid by Zhongdai Group Company, including the capital costs agreed between Dabao Company and Zhongdai Telecom Company. After repeated negotiations, Zhongdai Telecom Company, Zhongdai Group Company, and Zhongshan Company failed to refund the funds to Dabao Company, and Dabao Company thus filed this lawsuit.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court held in the first instance: The Cooperation Agreement entered into by Dabao Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company did not violate legal provisions and was lawful and valid; the parties should perform it accordingly. Dabao Company had performed its obligation to pay the first installment of the equity transfer price as agreed, which was used to pay the land transfer fee for the involved land parcel. However, Zhongdai Telecom Company failed to provide the target land parcel as agreed, rendering the purpose of the cooperation unattainable, which constituted a breach. Therefore, Dabao Company's request to rescind the Cooperation Agreement based on this fact and to order Zhongdai Telecom Company, Zhongshan Company, and Zhongdai Group Company to refund the RMB 30 million transfer payment was well-founded and had contractual and legal basis, and should be supported. Zhongdai Telecom Company, Zhongshan Company, and Zhongdai Group Company argued that Dabao Company's notice of rescission sent before the expiration of the three-month period stipulated in the contract constituted a breach by Dabao Company. Although Dabao Company proposed to rescind the contract before the three-month period under the Cooperation Agreement expired, Dabao Company's action had sufficient factual basis and was an exercise of its rights in accordance with the law. Therefore, this Court did not accept the argument of Zhongdai Telecom Company, Zhongshan Company, and Zhongdai Group Company, as it was inconsistent with the facts. Regarding the issue of compensation for losses, because the Cooperation Agreement stipulated that if the parties failed to reach an agreement on the cooperation matters within three months after the signing of the agreement (the cooperation parties formally signing an agreement on the cooperation matters concerning the target land parcel), Dabao Company had the right to withdraw from the cooperation, and Zhongdai Telecom Company agreed to acquire Dabao Company's 10% shares in Zhongshan Company for RMB 52.85 million and pay the full transfer price to Dabao Company immediately. Therefore, according to this agreement, under the circumstances where it was impossible to formally sign and perform the agreement on the cooperation matters, Dabao Company's claim that Zhongdai Telecom Company should compensate for the expected profit loss of RMB 22.85 million in addition to the RMB 30 million refund conformed to the true intentions of the parties and was supported by this Court. Additionally, the contract also stipulated that if Zhongdai Telecom Company defaulted, it must pay liquidated damages for overdue payment at a rate of 0.2% per day on the amount promised. However, Dabao Company waived the higher interest rate agreed in the contract and instead claimed interest at the overdue loan interest rate stipulated by the People's Bank of China for the same period, which was an exercise of its own rights and should be permitted. Dabao Company's request to calculate the above interest from February 23, 2006, the date it exercised its legitimate right to propose rescission, was in accordance with legal provisions, and the interest should be calculated from the day after the date it proposed rescission. Zhongshan Company should bear joint and several liability for Zhongdai Telecom Company's debts in accordance with the contract. Zhongdai Group Company, in the letters of commitment it issued to Dabao Company on two occasions, expressed its willingness to repay Zhongdai Telecom Company's debts. In the second letter of commitment (dated June 9, 2006), it expressly stated that the scope of its liability was to refund the land transfer fee paid by Dabao Company, i.e., the aforementioned RMB 30 million transfer payment, and the capital costs agreed between Dabao Company and Zhongdai Telecom Company. Moreover, because Dabao Company, while accepting Zhongdai Group Company's intention, did not waive its claims against Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company, Zhongdai Group Company's conduct constituted a joinder of debt, and it should assume liability for refunding the RMB 30 million and compensating for the expected profit loss to Dabao Company in accordance with the content of its commitment.

Regarding the issue of litigation parties. Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongdai Group Company argued that Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, shareholders of Zhongshan Company, had a legal interest in this case and applied to join them as third parties to clarify the facts. This Court held that the Cooperation Agreement was entered into by Dabao Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company. The rights and obligations under the agreement only concerned Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company. Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong were not parties to the agreement, and Dabao Company did not seek to hold them liable. If Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company believed that the actions of Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong had harmed their lawful rights and interests, they should resolve the matter separately. Therefore, these two natural persons were not necessary parties to this case. The requests of Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company lacked sufficient legal and factual basis and were not supported by this Court. Zhongshan Company argued that the Guangzhou Land Bureau's unilateral withdrawal of the target land parcel was the factual cause of the inability to perform the Cooperation Agreement and the failure to achieve the purpose of the contract, and thus applied to join that bureau as a third party in the litigation. In this regard, even if the conduct of the Guangzhou Land Bureau caused Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company to be unable to fulfill their contractual obligations, pursuant to Article 121 of the Contract Law, Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company must resolve the dispute between them and that bureau separately in accordance with the law. Therefore, Zhongshan Company's application did not comply with legal provisions and was rejected by this Court. On June 1, 2007, this Court rendered a judgment (2006) Sui Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 217, ordering: 1. Rescission of the Cooperation Agreement entered into by Dabao Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company. 2. Zhongdai Telecom Company shall, within ten days of the judgment taking effect, return the equity transfer payment of RMB 30 million and compensate for the expected profit loss of RMB 22.85 million to Dabao Company, and pay overdue payment interest on a principal of RMB 52.85 million from February 24, 2006, until the date of full payment, calculated at the overdue loan interest rate for the same period stipulated by the People's Bank of China. In case of delayed performance, execution shall be carried out in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law. 3. Zhongshan Company and Zhongdai Group Company shall bear joint and several liability for the debts Zhongdai Telecom Company is obligated to pay under item 2 of this judgment. 4. Rejection of Dabao Company's other claims. The case acceptance fee of RMB 285,050 and the property preservation fee of RMB 222,895 shall be jointly borne by Zhongdai Telecom Company, Zhongshan Company, and Zhongdai Group Company.

Zhongdai Group Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of the first instance, appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court, arguing: First, the court of first instance failed to notify a third party with a legal interest in the case to participate in the proceedings, omitting litigation subjects and causing procedural errors. The dispute in this case arose from Zhongdai Telecom Company's disposition of the equity in Zhongshan Company. However, the shareholders of Zhongshan Company are not Zhongdai Telecom Company, but Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong. Whether it is the equity disposition itself or the outcome of the case, it is closely related to the interests of the shareholders Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong. The land parcel to be developed involved in this case was obtained by Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong from the land administration department through an auction, and its subsequent recovery due to their failure to pay the land transfer fee in time led to Daba Company's unilateral rescission of the equity transfer agreement. According to the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, these two shareholders should participate in the proceedings as third parties, which would also help clarify the facts and distinguish right from wrong, as well as determine each party's fault and the apportionment of liability. Second, the court of first instance's determination that Daba Company incurred an expected profit loss of RMB 22.85 million lacks factual and legal basis. The equity transfer agreement stipulated: The transfer price for Daba Company to acquire 10% of the equity in Zhongshan Company was RMB 49.31 million; by December 13, 2005, Daba Company was to pay Zhongdai Telecom Company an initial installment of RMB 30 million for the equity, with the balance to be paid in full by December 30, 2005; Zhongshan Company could accept shareholder loans, with interest calculated at an annual rate of 25%; if the parties failed to reach an agreement on cooperation within three months after signing the agreement, Daba Company had the right to withdraw from the cooperation, and Zhongdai Telecom Company agreed to acquire Daba Company's 10% equity in Zhongshan Company for RMB 52.85 million. It can be seen that, in the event the cooperation could not be completed, the precondition for Daba Company to receive the withdrawal payment of RMB 52.85 million was the full payment of the 10% equity transfer price of RMB 49.31 million, with the remaining RMB 3.54 million being interest calculated at an annual rate of 25%. However, the facts of this case show that, after paying the initial installment of RMB 30 million, Daba Company failed to pay the second installment of RMB 19.31 million as agreed. This not only indicates that Daba Company breached the contract first, causing the land use right obtained through auction to be recovered by the government, but also that Daba Company never fully paid the equity transfer price. Therefore, its so-called "expected profit loss" has no contractual or factual basis. The equity transfer contract of Zhongshan Company should have been valid only if signed between the shareholders of Zhongshan Company, Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, and the equity transferee, Daba Company, and the industrial and commercial registration change for the equity transfer was completed. However, Zhongdai Telecom Company and Daba Company, without authorization or confirmation from Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, signed an agreement, which should be deemed an illegal act of disposing of others' rights and interests. This agreement should be deemed invalid, and Daba Company's claim for so-called expected profit loss based on an invalid contract lacks legal basis. Third, the court of first instance erred in ordering Zhongdai Group Company to bear joint and several liability. The "Letter of Commitment" issued by Zhongdai Group Company to Daba Company on December 12, 2005, was an invitation by Zhongdai Group Company for Daba Company to cooperate in operating Zhongshan Company and the land parcel to be acquired, and it expressed the hope that Daba Company would prepare RMB 30 million in funds before the parties finalized the cooperation terms, for use in paying the land transfer fee. However, thereafter, Daba Company did not sign any contract with Zhongdai Group Company but instead signed an agreement with Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company, and paid the initial installment of RMB 30 million for the equity based on that agreement. It can be seen that the "Letter of Commitment" from Zhongdai Group Company was essentially a letter of intent for an agreement, which received no response and does not have legal binding force. The "Letter of Commitment" issued by Zhongdai Group Company on June 9, 2006, was a proposal by Zhongdai Group Company that Zhongdai Group Company would be responsible for repaying the RMB 30 million and funding costs owed by Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company to Daba Company. The legal significance of this proposal is a transfer of debt. However, Daba Company did not respond but instead chose litigation. Zhongdai Group Company and Daba Company did not reach an agreement on the debt transfer. Daba Company's request for Zhongdai Group Company to bear joint and several liability with Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company has no contractual or legal basis. Therefore, it requested: 1. To set aside the judgment of the first instance and either remand the case for retrial or render a new judgment based on the facts as ascertained, dismissing Daba Company's claims. 2. To have Daba Company bear all litigation costs for the first and second instances.

Daba Company did not submit a written defense. During the investigation by the court of second instance, it made an oral defense stating: First, the judgment of the first instance did not involve the issue of omitting litigation subjects. The relationship between Zhongdai Telecom Company and Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong is not within the scope of adjustment of this case, and Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong do not need to participate in this litigation. Second, according to the terms of the "Cooperation Agreement," Zhongdai Telecom Company should acquire Daba Company's 10% equity in Zhongshan Company for RMB 52.85 million. Daba Company's calculation of expected profit loss based on this has a contractual basis. Third, Zhongdai Group Company's issuance of the letter of commitment constituted an act of debt joining, not a debt transfer. Zhongdai Group Company's assertion that because Daba Company chose to claim its creditor's rights against Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company, it has no right to claim against Zhongdai Group Company, has no basis. Therefore, it requested that Zhongdai Group Company's appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company did not participate in the court investigation of the second instance and did not submit written opinions.

The Guangdong High People's Court found the following facts upon retrial: In the "Cooperation Agreement," Daba Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company agreed that the transfer price for the 10% equity of Zhongshan Company to be transferred by Zhongdai Telecom Company was RMB 49.31 million. After the equity transfer, Zhongdai Telecom Company would hold 90% of the equity in Zhongshan Company, and Daba Company would hold 10%. The payment method for the equity transfer price was: By December 13, 2005, Daba Company would pay Zhongdai Telecom Company an initial installment of RMB 30 million for the equity, which would be used to pay the land transfer fee for the target land parcel, with the balance to be paid in full to Zhongdai Telecom Company by December 30, 2005. On December 13, 2005, Zhongshan Company issued a "Receipt" to Daba Company, stating that it had received RMB 30 million in investment funds from Daba Company. On the same day, Zhongshan Company remitted RMB 30 million to the Guangzhou Municipal Land Transfer Fee Financial Special Account. On February 23, 2006, Daba Company sent a letter to Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company stating: Because the target land parcel had been recovered by the government due to the failure to pay the land transfer fee on time, Daba Company and Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company could no longer reach an agreement on cooperation. Therefore, Daba Company formally notified them through this letter of the termination of the cooperation with Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company, and requested that Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company return Daba Company's funds as soon as possible in accordance with the agreement. On June 9, 2006, the "Letter of Commitment" issued by Zhongdai Group Company to Daba Company stated: Daba Company cooperated with Zhongdai Telecom Company, a subsidiary of Zhongdai Group Company, in operating Zhongshan Company (developing the PZB1301 land parcel located south of the new Canton Fair Complex in Pazhou). Since the land parcel had been recovered by the Guangzhou Land Administration Bureau, the RMB 30 million that Daba Company had originally paid as the state-owned land transfer fee would be repaid by Zhongdai Group Company, including the funding costs agreed upon between Daba Company and Zhongdai Telecom Company.

It was also found: On October 14, 2005, the Guangzhou Land Administration Bureau, as the transferor, and Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, as the transferees, signed the "State-owned Land Use Right Transfer Contract for Guangzhou City," transferring the Pazhou PZB1301 land parcel to Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong by way of listing for RMB 460 million. On October 25, 2005, Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong signed the "Articles of Association of Guangzhou Zhongshan Industrial Co., Ltd." and established Zhongshan Company. On December 5, 2005, Zhongshan Company was registered and established with the Guangzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce, with a registered capital of RMB 20 million and Zhang Weishan as its legal representative.

During the first-instance proceedings, Zhongshan Company submitted a "Reply to Suiguofanghan [2005] No. 1616," the main content of which was: "Guangzhou Land Resources and Housing Administration Bureau, The letter 'Regarding the Rescission of the Pazhou PZB1301 Land Parcel Transfer Contract' (Suiguofanghan [2005] No. 1616) was sent by your bureau to us, Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, by mail on December 29, 2005. We do not agree with your bureau's unilateral rescission of the Pazhou PZB1301 land parcel transfer contract. As natural persons purchasing land, we need time to register a project company and other matters. We had already paid the land transfer fee of RMB 73.8 million (and a one-time deed tax of RMB 13.8 million) before the contractually agreed date of December 14. Within less than 12 hours after our payment, your bureau made a unilateral decision to rescind the contract on December 15, and on December 20, your bureau issued a payment slip for the land transfer fee for us to pay. However, we did not receive your bureau's official letter of unilateral rescission until 15 days later (December 29). We believe that your bureau's decision, made within 12 hours regarding an enterprise, is somewhat inappropriate... Zhongshan Company, Xia Chengfeng, Su Xiong. January 12, 2006."

The Guangzhou Land Administration Bureau, on the grounds that Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong had violated the contract by failing to pay the land transfer fee on time, rescinded the "State-owned Land Use Right Transfer Contract for Guangzhou City" signed with them, recovered the Pazhou PZB1301 land parcel that had been transferred to Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, and re-auctioned it publicly through the Guangzhou Real Estate Transaction Registration Center on January 14, 2006.

Except for the above facts, the facts found by the Guangdong High People's Court upon retrial are the same as those found in the judgment of the first instance.

The Guangdong High People's Court held in the second instance: Based on the appeal requests of Zhongdai Group Company, the focus of the dispute between the parties is, first, whether Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong should be added as third parties to participate in the proceedings; and second, the issue of liability of Zhongdai Group Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company after the rescission of the "Cooperation Agreement."

Regarding the issue of whether Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong should be added as third parties to participate in the proceedings. The court held that the "Cooperation Agreement" signed by Zhongdai Telecom Company, Zhongshan Company, and Daba Company was the true expression of the parties' intentions. The purpose of signing this contract was to jointly develop real estate on the Pazhou PZB1301 land parcel. Its essence was to achieve the purpose of cooperative real estate development in the form of an equity transfer. The basis for the parties' cooperation was Zhongshan Company's acquisition of the land use right for the land parcel. According to the facts found, after signing the "State-owned Land Use Right Transfer Contract for Guangzhou City" with the Guangzhou Land Administration Bureau, Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong established Zhongshan Company and paid part of the funds to the Guangzhou Land Transfer Fee Financial Special Account in the name of Zhongshan Company. Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong are shareholders and directors of Zhongshan Company. Zhang Weishan, the legal representative of Zhongshan Company, was also directly employed by Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong. The RMB 30 million involved in this case was also paid by Zhongshan Company as the land transfer fee. Therefore, Zhongshan Company's signing of the "Cooperation Agreement" with Daba Company should be deemed to have been done under the entrustment of Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong and is legally valid. Because Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong failed to pay the land transfer fee on time, the Guangzhou Land Administration Bureau recovered the Pazhou PZB1301 land parcel and re-auctioned it publicly. The basis for the cooperative development of the real estate project by Zhongdai Telecom Company, Zhongshan Company, and Daba Company no longer exists, and the purpose of the contract cannot be achieved. Therefore, the "Cooperation Agreement" signed by them should be rescinded. The "Cooperation Agreement" was signed by Zhongdai Telecom Company, Zhongshan Company, and Daba Company. This case only concerns the issue of liability after the rescission of the contract. Daba Company did not assert its rights against Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong in this case. Therefore, there is no need to add Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong as third parties to participate in the proceedings. Zhongdai Group Company's appeal argument that the court of first instance failed to notify Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong as third parties to participate in the proceedings constitutes an omission of litigation subjects and a procedural error, which the court does not support.

Regarding the issue of liability of Zhongdai Group Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company after the rescission of the "Cooperation Agreement." The court held that Daba Company had paid the initial installment of RMB 30 million for the equity as agreed. However, Zhongdai Telecom Company failed to provide the target land parcel as promised, rendering the purpose of the cooperation unattainable. Therefore, Zhongdai Telecom Company should bear the corresponding liability for breach of contract. Daba Company's request for rescission of the contract, return of the RMB 30 million, and compensation for corresponding losses should be supported. According to the terms of the "Cooperation Agreement," Daba Company was to obtain 10% of the equity in Zhongshan Company by paying RMB 49.31 million to Zhongdai Telecom Company in two installments. Because the target land parcel was recovered, Daba Company actually only paid the initial installment of RMB 30 million for the equity and did not pay the second installment of RMB 19.31 million to Zhongdai Telecom Company. Therefore, the amount actually payable by Zhongdai Telecom Company after Daba Company's withdrawal from the cooperation should be determined based on the proportion of the paid RMB 30 million to the total payable RMB 49.31 million, i.e., 3000 ÷ 4931 × 5285 = RMB 32,153,721. According to the "Cooperation Agreement," from the date three months after the signing of the agreement, i.e., from March 13, 2006, Zhongdai Telecom Company should have paid this amount in full. Therefore, as agreed by the parties, from that date until the date of full payment, liquidated damages should be calculated at 0.2% per day on the principal of RMB 32,153,721. The method of calculation agreed in the "Cooperation Agreement" already exceeds the method of calculation claimed by Daba Company (which was based on a principal of RMB 52.85 million from February 24, 2006, until the date of full payment, at the overdue loan interest rate for the same period stipulated by the People's Bank of China for overdue payment of liquidated damages; Daba Company's claimed method was premised on compensation for expected profit loss of RMB 22.85 million). Although Daba Company only paid the first installment of the equity transfer price of RMB 30 million as agreed, the cooperative land parcel had already been recovered before the due date for the second installment, i.e., December 30, 2005. Therefore, Daba Company's failure to pay the remaining equity transfer price should be deemed an exercise of the right of defense for insecurity. Zhongdai Telecom Company, Zhongdai Group Company, and Zhongshan Company also did not raise or provide evidence to prove that Daba Company was unable to pay the amount. Therefore, it should be determined that Daba Company was not at fault in the rescission of the contract in this case. Considering that Daba Company has waived its right to claim compensation for losses according to the higher method of calculation agreed in the contract, this case can calculate the expected profit loss and corresponding compensation for losses according to Daba Company's claim, and item 2 of the judgment of the first instance can be affirmed. The court does not support Zhongdai Group Company's appeal argument that the agreement is invalid and that Daba Company's claim for expected profit loss based on an invalid contract has no legal basis.

Zhongshan Company, according to the terms of the "Cooperation Agreement," should bear joint and several liability for Zhongdai Telecom Company's debts. Zhongdai Group Company twice issued written commitments to Daba Company to be responsible for repaying Zhongdai Telecom Company's debts. This constitutes a voluntary assumption of debts. The court of first instance correctly characterized it as a debt joining. After the court of first instance rendered its judgment, Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company did not appeal. Zhongdai Group Company's appeal argument that this case should be characterized as a debt transfer is inconsistent with the facts and lacks legal basis, and the court also does not accept it. The court held that the court of first instance's findings of fact were clear, and the judgment was correct and should be affirmed. On December 3, 2007, the court rendered its judgment (2007) Yue Gao Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 165: Appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 285,050 was borne by Zhongdai Group Company.

After the second-instance judgment, Zhongdai Group Company, dissatisfied with the judgment, applied to this court for retrial. This court referred its application materials to the Guangdong High People's Court for review on March 4, 2008. Zhongdai Group Company requested that the second-instance judgment be set aside and Daba Company's claims be dismissed. The reasons were: First, the proceedings in the first and second instances were procedurally defective. The courts of first and second instance knew that the dispute between the Guangzhou Land Administration Bureau and Zhongshan Company would directly determine the outcome of this case, yet they did not add the Guangzhou Land Administration Bureau as a party. Moreover, they did not include the shareholders of Zhongshan Company as parties in this case, which was a procedural error. Second, the findings of fact in the first and second instance judgments were erroneous. Equity transfers should be made by shareholders. In this case, significant changes occurred in the equity of Zhongshan Company without any knowledge of all shareholders and were affirmed as valid, which is erroneous. The "Cooperation Agreement" concerned the specific transfer of equity in Zhongshan Company after its restructuring. However, Daba Company never submitted evidence regarding the equity of Zhongshan Company after the restructuring. Since the premise of the equity after such restructuring did not exist, the conditions attached to it were not established. According to the Company Law and the articles of association of Zhongshan Company, a transfer of company equity must be passed by a resolution of the shareholders' meeting and agreed by all shareholders before it can proceed. However, no such evidence was presented in the case. The floor price clause agreed in the above-mentioned equity transfer cooperation agreement is invalid. The clause "transfer of equity without reaching agreement on the company's articles of association" is an invalid contractual term that actually harms shareholders' rights. On December 13, 2005, the "Contract for the Transfer and Cooperation of Equity in Guangzhou Zhongshan Industrial Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Cooperation Contract") signed by Daba Company and Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong negated the "Cooperation Agreement" and re-stipulated the rights and obligations of the parties. Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong are the shareholders of Zhongshan Company and have all decision-making power over the company. Zhongdai Telecom Company has no legal relationship with Zhongshan Company and is not a shareholder of Zhongshan Company. The original judgments of the first and second instances erroneously found that Zhongdai Telecom Company had the right to dispose of 100% of the equity in Zhongshan Company. The legal representative of Zhongshan Company, Zhang Weishan, was actually an employee and had no right to decide on any matters concerning the company's equity. The findings of the first and second instance judgments that Zhongshan Company signed the cooperation agreement with Daba Company under the entrustment of Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong are not supported by evidence. Daba Company also failed to pay the remaining RMB 19.31 million to Zhongdai Telecom Company before December 30, 2005, and should bear liability for breach of contract. During the performance of the contract, Daba Company only paid the initial installment of RMB 30 million and did not pay the balance. It also did not complete the registration change for the equity transfer, meaning it did not hold 10% of the equity in Zhongshan Company. Its request for Zhongdai Telecom Company to acquire the non-existent 10% equity at a price of RMB 52.85 million lacks factual basis. The second-instance judgment, using RMB 32,153,721 as the principal and calculating liquidated damages at 0.2% per day from March 13, 2006, until the date of full payment, where 0.2% per day is equivalent to 6% per month or 72% per year, and supporting this calculation even when the party argued that the liquidated damages were excessively high, is unfair. Third, the application of law in the first and second instance judgments was improper. Due to the procedural defects and erroneous findings of fact in the first and second instance judgments, the law could not be correctly and accurately applied.

Dabao Company primarily argued in its defense: 1. The procedures of the first and second instance trials were lawful. Dabao Company's claim for compensation from Zhongdai Telecom Company and for Zhongshan Company to assume guarantee liability, based on the contract entered into by the parties, had sufficient factual and legal basis. Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong had no relationship with this case. The legality of the Guangzhou Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources' withdrawal of the land was not within the scope of trial of this case. The "Cooperation Agreement" signed by Dabao Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company was legally valid. Dabao Company did not sign a "Cooperation Contract" with Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong. The amount of compensation that Dabao Company requested from Zhongdai Telecom Company was reasonable and legal.

The facts found by the Guangdong High People's Court upon review were consistent with the facts found in the second instance judgment. During the period of appeal, Zhongdai Group Company submitted a "Cooperation Contract" signed by Xia Chengfeng, Su Xiong, and Dabao Company on December 13, 2005, which provided: 1. Shareholder equity transfer and restructuring of Zhongshan Company. (1) Shareholder Xia Chengfeng held 85% of the equity in Zhongshan Company, with a capital contribution of RMB 17 million, of which 50% of the equity was to be transferred to Dabao Company, i.e., the transfer consideration for 50% of the equity at par value was RMB 10 million. (2) Shareholder Su Xiong held 15% of the equity in Zhongshan Company, with a capital contribution of RMB 3 million, all of which was to be transferred to Dabao Company, i.e., the transfer consideration for 15% of the equity at par value was RMB 3 million. (3) After the transfer, the equity ratio of Zhongshan Company would be: Dabao Company 65%, Xia Chengfeng 35%. (4) After restructuring, both shareholders agreed to make equity changes and management adjustments to Zhongshan Company. The parties agreed that the equity change would be registered with the industry and commerce administration when the total construction area of the development project on the target land (Pazhou PZB1301 plot) reached 60%, and the board of directors of Zhongshan Company would be adjusted accordingly. After the adjustment, the board of directors of Zhongshan Company would consist of five directors, of whom Dabao Company would appoint three and Xia Chengfeng would appoint two. (5) From the date of signing this contract, the "Cooperation Agreement" signed by Dabao Company and Zhongdai Telecom Company would automatically lapse, the paid amount would be treated as the equity transfer consideration under the "Cooperation Contract," and the balance would be used as part of the payment for the land transfer fee. 2. Payment method for the equity transfer consideration. (1) On December 13, 2005, the transferee, Dabao Company, was required to transfer the consideration for Xia Chengfeng's 50% equity, in the amount of RMB 10 million, into the account of Zhongshan Company. (2) On December 13, 2005, the transferee, Dabao Company, was required to transfer the consideration for Su Xiong's 15% equity, in the amount of RMB 3 million, into the account of Zhongshan Company. (3) As of December 12, 2005, Zhongshan Company had completed its accounting, had no claims or debts, and both parties had acknowledged this. From the date of signing this contract, Dabao Company became a shareholder of Zhongshan Company, enjoying shareholder rights and assuming obligations and liabilities in accordance with Article 3 of the Company Law. 3. Payment of land transfer fee and deed tax. (1) After restructuring, the shareholders would use Zhongshan Company as an operating platform to jointly develop the real estate project on the target land for mutual benefit. The target land was offered for sale by public listing on October 14, 2005. The land plot was named Pazhou PZB1301, located in Zone B of Pazhou Island, Haizhu District, with an area of 24,862 square meters and a total floor area of ≤ 73,925 square meters. The transfer fee for the target land was RMB 460 million, and the deed tax was RMB 13.8 million. Both shareholders would pay the land transfer fee and deed tax in accordance with the payment schedule stipulated in the "Guangzhou State-owned Land Use Right Transfer Contract" (Contract No. Sui Guo Di Chu He [2005] No. 133). (2) Both shareholders agreed to pay the land transfer fee and deed tax as follows: The first installment of the land transfer fee, RMB 200 million, was to be paid before December 14, 2005, of which shareholder Dabao Company would pay RMB 170 million and shareholder Xia Chengfeng would pay RMB 30 million (including the auction deposit of RMB 10 million). The second installment of the land transfer fee, RMB 260 million, was to be paid before April 14, 2006, of which shareholder Dabao Company would pay RMB 129 million and shareholder Xia Chengfeng would pay RMB 131 million. The land deed tax of RMB 13.8 million was to be paid within the time limit notified by the government, of which shareholder Dabao Company would pay RMB 8.97 million and shareholder Xia Chengfeng would pay RMB 4.83 million. (3) The shareholders could directly transfer the land transfer fee to the dedicated fiscal account for land transfer fees of the Guangzhou Municipal Government, with the account opened at the Head Office of Guangzhou Commercial Bank, account number 328-8000545-55, or transfer it into the account of Zhongshan Company, which would then forward it to the dedicated fiscal account. (4) The parties agreed on liquidated damages: The shareholders must ensure that the first installment of the land transfer fee was paid in full before December 14, 2005. If one shareholder failed to pay or failed to pay the full amount on time, that shareholder would pay 50% of the total amount of the first installment of the land transfer fee as economic compensation to the complying shareholder, and bear the direct economic losses and legal liability arising therefrom. 4. The dividends of the company would be calculated from the date of signing the contract. The transferor would enjoy dividends before the transfer, and the transferee would enjoy dividends after the transfer. 5. From the date of transfer, Su Xiong would no longer be a shareholder of the company and could not engage in any activities externally in the company's name. The contract was made in five copies, one submitted to the company registration authority, one held by each shareholder, and one kept on file by the company, all having equal legal effect. The contract would take effect upon signature by the transferor and transferee.

Dabao Company denied having signed the aforesaid "Cooperation Contract" with Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong.

The Guangdong High People's Court found upon review: Dabao Company filed the lawsuit based on the cooperative operating agreement it signed with Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company, seeking an order for Zhongdai Telecom Company to compensate for losses and for Zhongshan Company to assume guarantee liability, and did not assert claims against Xia Chengfeng or Su Xiong. The original first instance and second instance judgments found that there was no need to join Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong in the proceedings, and such handling was not improper. Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong were shareholders and directors of Zhongshan Company. Zhongshan Company received the RMB 30 million paid by Dabao Company pursuant to the "Cooperation Agreement" and used the funds to pay part of the land transfer fee that Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong were required to pay. The second instance judgment found that Zhongshan Company's signing of the "Cooperation Agreement" was done on behalf of and as authorized by its shareholders Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, which was consistent with the facts. In the contract signed by Dabao Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company, the transfer involved 10% of the equity in Zhongshan Company, with a transfer consideration of RMB 30 million. However, the "Cooperation Contract" submitted by Zhongdai Group Company during the appeal period provided for the transfer of 50% and 15% of the equity in Zhongshan Company held by Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong respectively, with prices of RMB 10 million and RMB 3 million respectively. Based on the facts found, Dabao Company performed its obligations under the "Cooperation Agreement" it signed with Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company, which was confirmed in the commitment letter issued by Zhongdai Group Company to Dabao Company on June 9, 2006. Because Dabao Company denied having signed the "Cooperation Contract" with Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, and Zhongdai Group Company failed to provide evidence proving that the contract had been actually performed (such as payment of transfer consideration and registration of equity change), its claim that the "Cooperation Contract" had replaced the "Cooperation Agreement" was insufficiently supported by evidence and was not accepted. The calculation method for liquidated damages in the second instance judgment did not violate the contract provisions or legal requirements. Zhongdai Group Company's application did not meet the conditions set forth in Article 179, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law. The Guangdong High People's Court, pursuant to Article 181, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, ruled to reject Zhongdai Group Company's application for retrial.

Zhongdai Group Company, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, the second instance judgment, and the ruling of the Guangdong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the "Guangdong High Court Ruling"), appealed to this Court, arguing: 1. The first instance judgment, the second instance judgment, and the Guangdong High Court Ruling violated statutory procedures by not joining Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, which was erroneous. Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong were the only two shareholders of Zhongshan Company. Both the "Cooperation Agreement" and the "Cooperation Contract" involved the transfer of the equity held by these two individuals, but the contents of the two contracts were inconsistent. The validity or invalidity of either contract would have a significant impact on the interests of these two individuals. The outcome of the case had a legal interest relationship with Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong. Pursuant to Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law, the court should have added Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong as third parties. The Guangzhou Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources should also have been added as a party to the case. 2. The "Cooperation Agreement" should be deemed invalid. (1) The transfer of equity should be conducted by the shareholders themselves. The parties entitled to transfer the equity of Zhongshan Company were Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong. However, the "Cooperation Agreement" disposed of the equity without the authorization of Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, by Zhongdai Telecom Company, Dabao Company, and Zhongshan Company. This constituted unauthorized disposition and should be invalid. (2) The "Cooperation Agreement" was for the purpose of developing a real estate project, but the signatories lacked development qualifications. (3) The Guangdong High Court Ruling and the second instance judgment found that Zhongshan Company's signing of the "Cooperation Agreement" was on behalf of and as authorized by Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, based on the facts that Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong were shareholders of Zhongshan Company, that Zhongshan Company received the RMB 30 million from Dabao Company pursuant to the "Cooperation Agreement," and that Zhongshan Company used the funds to pay the land transfer fee that Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong were required to pay. This finding was erroneous. The "Cooperation Agreement" did not state that Zhongshan Company was acting on behalf of Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong in disposing of their equity, nor was there any other evidence proving the existence of an agency relationship between the two parties. Moreover, Article 5 of the "Cooperation Agreement" identified the seller of the equity as Zhongdai Telecom Company, not Zhongshan Company. Therefore, the conclusion that Zhongshan Company was authorized by Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong to transfer the equity could not stand. Additionally, there was no logical connection between Zhongshan Company's authorized transfer of equity and its receipt of funds and payment of land transfer fees. The inference drawn by the Guangdong High Court Ruling based on these three factors was erroneous. In fact, the actions of Zhongshan Company receiving the funds and Dabao Company making the payment were not performance of the "Cooperation Agreement" but performance of the "Cooperation Contract." The "Cooperation Agreement" provided that Dabao Company was to pay Zhongdai Telecom Company, but in this case, Dabao Company actually paid Zhongshan Company, which was consistent with the terms of the "Cooperation Contract." The "Cooperation Contract" provided that the amount paid by Dabao Company would be treated as equity transfer consideration and the balance as part of the payment for the land transfer fee. Whether the RMB 30 million paid by Zhongshan Company for the land transfer fee came from Dabao Company, and even if it did, had no bearing on whether Zhongshan Company was authorized by its shareholders to dispose of the equity. (4) The "Cooperation Agreement" violated the mandatory provisions of Article 72, paragraph 4 of the Company Law and should be invalid. (5) The provision in Article 11 of the "Cooperation Agreement" constituted a guaranteed minimum return clause and should be invalid. 3. Even if the "Cooperation Agreement" were valid, the subsequent "Cooperation Contract" was valid and therefore the "Cooperation Agreement" had been rescinded by the "Cooperation Contract." (1) The "Cooperation Contract" was signed by Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, shareholders of Zhongshan Company, and Dabao Company. It reflected the true intentions of all parties and should be legally valid. The "Cooperation Contract" rescinded the "Cooperation Agreement." Dabao Company also intended to seek benefits through the "Cooperation Contract," so the "Cooperation Contract" should have been reviewed and recognized in this case. (2) The Guangdong High Court Ruling, based on Dabao Company's denial of having signed the "Cooperation Contract" and Zhongdai Group Company's failure to provide evidence proving that the contract had been actually performed, found that the "Cooperation Contract" did not replace the "Cooperation Agreement." This finding was erroneous. Dabao Company did not provide evidence to prove that the "Cooperation Contract" was false, nor did it apply for an expert examination. The authenticity of the "Cooperation Contract" was not negated simply by Dabao Company's denial. Article 1(5) of the "Cooperation Contract" already provided that the "Cooperation Agreement" would automatically lapse. The "Cooperation Contract" had also been actually performed. Dabao Company's payment of RMB 30 million to Zhongshan Company was a manifestation of performance of the "Cooperation Contract." 4. Even if the "Cooperation Agreement" had not been rescinded, Dabao Company should be in breach of contract. (1) On the day after signing the "Cooperation Agreement," Dabao Company signed the "Cooperation Contract" with Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, whose content was contradictory to the former, and expressly provided that the "Cooperation Agreement" would automatically lapse. This caused the "Cooperation Agreement" to be impossible to perform and constituted a fundamental breach. This breach occurred before the land in question was withdrawn by the land department, so Dabao Company breached the contract first. (2) Article 6 of the "Cooperation Agreement" provided that Dabao Company should pay the first installment of the equity transfer consideration of RMB 30 million to Zhongdai Telecom Company before December 13, 2005, and pay the balance before December 30 of the same year. However, Zhongdai Telecom Company never received the equity transfer consideration from Dabao Company, constituting a breach by Dabao Company. 5. Even if Zhongdai Group Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company should bear liability for breach of contract, the unpaid RMB 19.31 million transfer consideration and the corresponding interest should be deducted. Article 5 of the "Cooperation Agreement" provided that the equity transfer consideration was RMB 49.31 million, and Article 11 provided that Zhongdai Telecom Company agreed to repurchase the 10% equity in Zhongshan Company held by Dabao Company for RMB 52.85 million. Thus, Dabao Company's expected benefit was RMB 3.54 million. After paying RMB 30 million, Dabao Company still owed RMB 19.31 million. Therefore, even if Zhongdai Group Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company repurchased the equity for RMB 52.85 million, the unpaid RMB 19.31 million should be deducted. Similarly, the principal amount for calculating the liquidated damages to be borne by the three companies should also deduct the RMB 19.31 million. The second instance judgment and the Guangdong High Court Ruling erroneously found that Dabao Company's expected benefit was RMB 22.85 million. 6. Zhongdai Group Company should not bear any liability; it did not constitute an assumption of debt. (1) The two commitments issued by Zhongdai Group Company were both directed at the "Cooperation Agreement." Since the agreement was invalid and not actually performed, the parties to that contract did not have any restitution obligation. Dabao Company's losses under that contract should be borne by itself. Therefore, Zhongdai Group Company should not be liable. (2) The "Commitment Letter" of June 9, 2006, was obtained by Dabao Company by intentionally concealing the existence of the "Cooperation Contract." This fraudulent conduct rendered the commitment invalid. (3) The RMB 30 million paid by Dabao Company was its performance under the "Cooperation Contract." Its restitution claim should be asserted against the parties to that contract and should be resolved in a separate case. In summary, Zhongdai Group Company requested that the Guangdong High Court Ruling, the first instance judgment, and the second instance judgment be set aside, that Dabao Company's claims be dismissed, and that Dabao Company bear the litigation costs.

Zhongdai Telecom Company, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, the second instance judgment, and the Guangdong High Court Ruling, appealed to this Court, making the same requests as Zhongdai Group Company. In addition to the grounds raised by Zhongdai Group Company, it further argued: The "Cooperation Agreement" was in name a cooperation but in substance a loan, constituting an inter-enterprise lending transaction, and should be invalid; Dabao Company did not actually pay RMB 30 million to Zhongdai Telecom Company; Dabao Company waived the calculation method of 0.2% daily liquidated damages when it filed the lawsuit at first instance, and the second instance judgment should not have used this to infer losses. Moreover, the conditions for Dabao Company to require Zhongdai Telecom Company to pay the equity transfer consideration under Article 11 of the "Cooperation Agreement" were not met, and the second instance judgment should not have used this as the basis for calculating liquidated damages. The rescission of the "Cooperation Agreement" was only determined as a fact after the court's judgment, so interest and liquidated damages should be calculated from the date Dabao Company filed the lawsuit.

Zhongshan Company, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, the second instance judgment, and the Guangdong High Court Ruling, appealed to this Court, making the same requests as Zhongdai Group Company. In addition to the grounds raised by Zhongdai Group Company, it further argued: The "Cooperation Agreement" was in name a cooperation but in substance a loan, constituting an inter-enterprise lending transaction, and should be invalid.

Dabao Company argued in its defense: 1. The first and second instance trial procedures were lawful. First, the purpose of the "Cooperation Agreement" was to restructure Zhongshan Company by way of equity transfer, and to use the restructured Zhongshan Company as a business platform to jointly develop the land involved in the lawsuit. The main rights and obligations stipulated in the "Cooperation Agreement" were to be assumed by Zhongdai Telecom Company and Dabao Company, with Zhongshan Company assisting Zhongdai Telecom Company in performing its obligations and guaranteeing Zhongdai Telecom Company's obligations under the "Cooperation Agreement." Dabao Company's claims and the facts on which they were based had no direct legal relationship with Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong. Although the equity changes stipulated in the "Cooperation Agreement" involved the equity transfer actions of Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, this was merely a condition promised by Zhongdai Telecom Company and an execution step in the restructuring of Zhongshan Company. When Zhongdai Telecom Company was unable to perform its obligations, Dabao Company could claim compensation for losses from it and require Zhongshan Company to assume the guarantee liability. Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong had no connection to the assumption of such legal liability, and there was no need to add these two persons as parties. Second, existing evidence had already proven that the land department had taken back the land involved in the lawsuit, which was sufficient. Whether the land department's recovery of the land was lawful concerned a different legal relationship and was irrelevant to this case. 2. Dabao Company did not sign the "Cooperation Contract" with Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong. This contract was forged by Zhongdai Group Company and was defective. First, during the retrial review by the Guangdong High People's Court, Dabao Company had already explained that after the "Cooperation Agreement" was signed, for the purpose of performing the agreement, Dabao Company had reserved equity transfer documents that were signed and sealed, and Zhongdai Group Company had forged these documents to create the "Cooperation Contract." This illegal act should be severely punished. In terms of form, if the "Cooperation Agreement" were to be amended, it should be done through consensus among all parties to that agreement. However, the signing parties of the "Cooperation Contract" were not identical to those of the aforementioned agreement, yet it purported to abolish the former agreement, which was unreasonable. All signing parties to the "Cooperation Agreement" had affixed cross-page seals, whereas the "Cooperation Contract," involving a huge sum, did not have cross-page seals or authorization from the legal representative. The main body of the "Cooperation Contract" also had no signatures or seals, and the signature and seal page at the end only contained simple content such as "for submission to the Bureau of Industry and Commerce for record," which could not be linked to the main body of the preceding pages. In terms of content, the "Cooperation Contract" required Dabao Company to pay the land transfer fee of RMB 170 million on the day of contracting, otherwise it would bear liability for breach of contract at 50% of the first installment of the land transfer fee of RMB 200 million, i.e., RMB 100 million. The contract also recorded that the equity change procedures would only be handled when the total building area reached 60% completion. It was impossible for Dabao Company to sign a contract with such severe breach of contract clauses. Moreover, even if it were signed, the equity change would not have been postponed. Second, there was no evidence in the case to confirm the existence and actual performance of the "Cooperation Contract," and it contradicted the content of evidence that had been confirmed. The petitioners in the original trial had all confirmed the authenticity of the "Cooperation Agreement," while the "Cooperation Contract" contradicted the content of the former agreement. The "Letter of Undertaking" issued by Zhongdai Group Company on June 9, 2006, was consistent with the content of the "Cooperation Agreement," which also indicated that the "Cooperation Contract" did not exist. Third, the "Cooperation Contract" did not qualify as new evidence under the Civil Procedure Law. If this contract were genuine, as key evidence, the petitioners should have submitted it during the first and second instance proceedings, but they did not submit it, which was unreasonable. Moreover, the "Cooperation Contract" was evidence that existed before the original trial, and there was no obstacle to its submission. Since the petitioners did not submit it in the original trial, this evidence should not be admitted in the retrial stage. 3. The first and second instance trials found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. From the content of the "Cooperation Agreement," it could be seen that the transfer of 10% equity in Zhongshan Company was merely a step in the cooperation among the parties. The "Cooperation Agreement" itself was not an equity transfer agreement, and its full performance required the coordination of other related agreements. This agreement could not be simply treated as an equity transfer agreement concerning Zhongshan Company. The equity changes involved in the agreement still required new agreements to be realized, which also confirmed the fact that Dabao Company had reserved the last page of the so-called "Cooperation Contract" for signing in relation to the equity transfer matters. Therefore, the "Cooperation Agreement" should be valid, and the judgments of the first and second instance trials were accurate. 4. Dabao Company's voluntary waiver of excessive compensation amounts was not illegal. According to Article 11 of the "Cooperation Agreement," after Dabao Company terminated the cooperation agreement, Zhongdai Telecom Company was required to acquire the equity corresponding to the amounts paid by Dabao Company for RMB 52.85 million and pay the full amount immediately; otherwise, it would pay liquidated damages at 0.2% per day on the unfulfilled amount. The amount of liquidated damages calculated according to this clause, calculated at the time of the first instance judgment, was RMB 29.85 million (default period of 460 days). The loss compensation of RMB 22.85 million plus overdue payment interest claimed by Dabao Company was less than the aforementioned amount. This was Dabao Company's disposal of its own rights and was not illegal. Moreover, Dabao Company had not recovered its funds, and its losses were greater than those of the petitioners. If liquidated damages were calculated at 0.2% per day until the date of payment, such damages would currently exceed RMB 100 million. Dabao Company had already waived a significant amount of liquidated damages from the petitioners. The amount of liquidated damages was also not a statutory ground for retrial, and the amount should not be adjusted during the retrial phase. In summary, Dabao Company requested the rejection of the petitioners' application for retrial and that corresponding liability be pursued against them.

We confirm the facts found by the Guangdong High People's Court in the second instance. During the retrial proceedings of this Court, the petitioners submitted to this Court the "Cooperation Contract," the content of which is consistent with the "Cooperation Contract" provided by Zhongdai Group Company during the retrial review by the Guangdong High People's Court.

Opinion of the Court: The "Cooperation Agreement" signed by Dabao Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company stipulated that the three parties would jointly develop the target land as real estate, and that Zhongdai Telecom Company would transfer 10% of its 100% equity in Zhongshan Company to Dabao Company. Although at the time of signing this agreement, the shareholders of Zhongshan Company were Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, and Zhongdai Telecom Company did not hold any equity in Zhongshan Company, the agreement only imposed an obligation on Zhongdai Telecom Company to transfer equity to Dabao Company, without allowing Dabao Company to actually obtain equity and thereby cause a change in Zhongshan Company's equity. The agreement also did not impose obligations on Zhongshan Company's shareholders, Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, nor did it infringe upon the equity rights of Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong in Zhongshan Company. Therefore, the "Cooperation Agreement" is not invalid due to the fact that Zhongdai Telecom Company was not a shareholder of Zhongshan Company. Because the "Cooperation Agreement" did not infringe upon the equity rights of Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong in Zhongshan Company, and Dabao Company did not assert claims against Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong have no legal interest in the handling of this case. The rescission of the land use right transfer contract signed by the Guangzhou Land Bureau with Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong belongs to a different legal relationship and does not affect Dabao Company's right to assert claims against Zhongdai Telecom Company under the "Cooperation Agreement." Therefore, the original trial court's decision not to add Xia Chengfeng, Su Xiong, and the Guangzhou Land Bureau as parties to the case was not improper. The "Cooperation Agreement" stipulated that Dabao Company would purchase equity in Zhongshan Company from Zhongdai Telecom Company to jointly develop the land involved in the lawsuit, and also stipulated that if no formal agreement on the land cooperation could be reached, Dabao Company had the right to withdraw from the cooperation. Subsequently, when Zhongshan Company did not obtain the right to use the land involved in the lawsuit and the land cooperation could not be realized, Dabao Company requested to withdraw from the cooperation. This indicates that at the time of signing the "Cooperation Agreement," Dabao Company's purpose was to acquire equity to participate in the development of the land and make a profit, not to lend funds to Zhongdai Telecom Company. The stipulation in Article 11 of the "Cooperation Agreement" that Zhongdai Telecom Company would buy back the equity for RMB 52.85 million was an arrangement set by the parties for Dabao Company's exit from the cooperation, and it does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and regulations. The "Cooperation Agreement" did not result in any actual change in the equity of Zhongshan Company, and the agreement does not violate the provisions of Article 72 of the Company Law. Whether the parties to the "Cooperation Agreement" possess real estate development qualifications may only affect the feasibility of performing the agreement, but does not affect the validity of the agreement. Therefore, the petitioners' claim that the "Cooperation Agreement" is invalid due to reasons such as it constituting a loan between enterprises, Article 11 being a minimum profit guarantee clause, violating relevant provisions of the Company Law, and the signing parties lacking real estate development qualifications, lacks factual and legal basis, and we do not support this claim. The "Cooperation Agreement" represents the true intention of each party, does not violate mandatory provisions of laws and regulations, and should be valid.

The "Cooperation Contract" provided by Zhongdai Group Company, Zhongdai Telecom Company, and Zhongshan Company records that it was signed between Dabao Company and the shareholders of Zhongshan Company, Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong, after the signing of the "Cooperation Agreement," and states that upon the signing of this contract, the "Cooperation Agreement" would automatically become void. Since the party named in the "Cooperation Contract," Dabao Company, denies the authenticity of the contract and claims that the contract was forged by the petitioners using relevant signing documents from the "Cooperation Agreement," the authenticity of the "Cooperation Contract" is unclear. For Dabao Company to render the "Cooperation Agreement" it signed void or to rescind the "Cooperation Agreement," it must express its intention to the parties of the "Cooperation Agreement." However, Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong are not parties to the "Cooperation Agreement," so even if the "Cooperation Contract" were genuine and valid, the stipulation therein that the "Cooperation Agreement" would automatically become void cannot achieve the effect of rescinding the "Cooperation Agreement." The petitioners' claim that the "Cooperation Contract" rescinded the "Cooperation Agreement" cannot be established, and we do not support this claim. Since Dabao Company did not assert claims against the petitioners based on the "Cooperation Contract," whether this contract is genuine and whether it was actually performed are separate issues unrelated to this case. We will not adjudicate the "Cooperation Contract."

The "Cooperation Agreement" stipulated that the initial installment of RMB 30 million for the equity transfer paid by Dabao Company to Zhongdai Telecom Company was to be used to pay the land transfer fee for the land involved in the lawsuit. Zhongshan Company confirmed that it actually received the RMB 30 million and used it for the purpose stipulated in the agreement. The "Letter of Undertaking" issued by Zhongdai Group Company on June 9, 2006, indicates that Dabao Company and Zhongdai Telecom Company were cooperating in the operation of Zhongshan Company and that Dabao Company had paid the land transfer fee of RMB 30 million. Zhongdai Telecom Company also did not argue that the use of this RMB 30 million to pay the land transfer fee violated the purpose of the payment stipulated in the "Cooperation Agreement." Therefore, it should be determined that Dabao Company paid the initial installment of RMB 30 million for the equity transfer to Zhongdai Telecom Company. The petitioners' claim that Dabao Company did not pay the equity transfer price to Zhongdai Telecom Company is difficult to establish, and we do not support it. Dabao Company's claim that it paid the initial installment of RMB 30 million for the equity transfer as stipulated in the "Cooperation Agreement" is confirmed by this Court.

Dabao Company and Zhongdai Telecom Company stipulated in the "Cooperation Agreement" that if the parties failed to formally sign an agreement on the cooperation regarding the land involved in the lawsuit within three months after signing this agreement, Dabao Company had the right to withdraw from the cooperation. In December 2005, the Guangzhou Land Bureau rescinded the land use right transfer contract signed with Xia Chengfeng and Su Xiong. Thereafter, Zhongshan Company did not actually obtain the right to use the land involved in the lawsuit, and Dabao Company and Zhongdai Telecom Company did not sign an agreement on the cooperation regarding the land involved in the lawsuit. Therefore, Dabao Company's withdrawal from the cooperation complies with the agreement between the parties. On February 23, 2006, Dabao Company sent a letter to Zhongdai Telecom Company and Zhongshan Company requesting termination of the cooperation with these two companies, which was not improper. Although the "Cooperation Agreement" stipulated that after Dabao Company withdrew from the cooperation, Zhongdai Telecom Company should buy back the 10% equity in Zhongshan Company held by Dabao Company for RMB 52.85 million, this stipulation was premised on Dabao Company having previously paid the full equity transfer price of RMB 49.31 million to Zhongdai Telecom Company. In this case, Dabao Company did not pay the full equity transfer price of RMB 49.31 million to Zhongdai Telecom Company, but only paid RMB 30 million. Therefore, Dabao Company's claim that Zhongdai Telecom Company should buy back the equity transferred by Zhongdai Telecom Company to Dabao Company for RMB 52.85 million lacks a factual basis, and we do not accept it. The second instance judgment's determination that, after Dabao Company withdrew from the cooperation, Zhongdai Telecom Company should return RMB 32,153,721 based on the proportion of the RMB 30 million paid by Dabao Company to the total payable amount of RMB 49.31 million lacked sufficient reasoning, and we correct this.
